threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stand on the wrong side of the escalator at the tube, looking confused when locals rush past. It's like a rite of passage.
Last night on the 196, a bloke serenaded the bus with old jazz tunes, and the driver clapped along. Only in Brixton, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting on the terrace, I heard the neighbor's cat and a street musician harmonizing. That's when I realized I belonged here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a bus in Friedrichshain, then, just as quickly, find yourself at an underground techno party while it's still daylight. That vibe is a Berlin special.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively know to avoid BART during rush hour—no amount of overhyped tech can change that chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a pigeon hop onto the 19 bus and somehow it seemed normal. Only in San Francisco do we have feathered commuters.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is always buzzing, but many afternoons it’s like a ghost town, the locals are inside enjoying their siestas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're the ones still taking a picture of the Casa Ramos sign like it’s a hidden gem, while locals just walk on by.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look puzzled when a bus driver calls you 'love' or 'darling'—trust me, it’s just part of the charm.
Last night on the 133, a couple was arguing about which chicken shop is better. It got so loud, even the driver joined in with a laugh.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a random guy in a chicken suit dancing outside the kiezkultur café while a samba band played in the background. Classic Neukölln vibes.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find a bus stop where the route's been suspended because of a protest, yet folks just sit there eating döner like it's normal.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their reaction to random BART outages; the eye roll is universal, especially during Friday evening crush.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 19 Polk, taking selfies like he was in a fashion show. Classic SF—always a party on the Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just grab brunch anytime; locals know that the good places in Gràcia close by 4 PM, so we plan our days around it.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with the T10 tickets at the metro machine, while locals swipe effortlessly by.
